issues.title: Bochner pairing uses the wrong integration domain

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any interval $J \subset \RR$, we consider the Bochner space $\Ltwosp{J, \HHilb}$
We fix some final time $T > 0$ and introduce the interval $I := (0, T)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed equation claims to define an inner product on L2(J,H) for every interval J, but its right-hand side integrates over [0,T]=I rather than J. Thus it may evaluate functions outside their domain or fail positive definiteness by ignoring part of J.
dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.overall_effect: The generic-J weak formulations and whole-line extension arguments are not well-defined under the displayed pairing, although the paper's core finite-time uses with J=I are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the definition of the Bochner inner product on L²(J,H), replace the integral over (0,T) by an integral over J, and read every L²(J,H) pairing accordingly. All formulas with J=I remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old sentence quantifies over an arbitrary interval J, and u and v are defined only on J, so the integration domain J is uniquely forced by the source and by standard Bochner-space notation. This single transcriptional correction makes every generic-J and whole-line use well-defined without repairing any argument or changing any guarantee.

issues.title: Initial condition names the wrong autonomous unknown

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we consider $u^{*,0}\in \Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}$ and $u^*\in \Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}$ the unique solutions

issues.failure_explanation: As written, the displayed system does not syntactically impose its initial datum on the named unknown u^{*,0}. The preceding declaration of u^{*,0} as the solution with data u0 makes u^{*,0}(0)=u0 the only coherent reading.
issues.overall_effect: This is a localized notational defect in the displayed autonomous initial-value problem; the surrounding text makes the intended data unambiguous, so no later formal argument needs alteration.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the initial condition u(0)=u₀ in the autonomous system by u^{*,0}(0)=u₀. No subsequent statement or proof needs modification.
issues.why_classification: The differential equation and the preceding declaration both name u^{*,0} as the autonomous unknown, making u^{*,0}(0)=u₀ the uniquely forced reading. The defect is purely transcriptional and no inference depends on the stray symbol.

issues.title: Whole-line extension is inadmissible under the old weak-solution definition

failure_location.quote: Define $\tilde u \in \Lloctwosp{\RR, \HHilb}$ as the unique solution to the evolution problem

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An element $u \in \Ltwosp{J, \HHilb}$ is said to be a weak solution

issues.failure_explanation: In the density proof, choose u^{*,0}(t)=e^{-itH}u0 on I with u0 nonzero and f=0. Its asserted whole-line extension is e^{-itH}u0 for negative times and has norm ||u0|| at every time, so it lies in L2_loc(R,H) but not L2(R,H). Consequently it cannot be the claimed solution “in the sense” of the old definition, and the proof's extension-and-mollification step is not justified.
dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.overall_effect: The supplied proof of density and the resulting integration-by-parts justification use an inadmissible whole-line object, affecting the later dual-formulation chain. The same old definition also makes the whole-line solution invoked in the time-regularity theorem unavailable for nonzero homogeneous data. Results confined to bounded I retain their intended solution class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For unbounded time intervals, define weak solutions in L²_loc(J,H), while retaining L²(J,H) on bounded intervals, and formulate the weak identity against compactly supported tests. Record the corresponding local Duhamel existence and uniqueness by restriction to bounded subintervals. Use this notion for both the extension with forcing 1_I f in the density proof and the whole-line solution in the smooth-potential theorem; the density, integration-by-parts, dual-formulation, L²-corollary, and time-regularity conclusions then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The global L² requirement is coherent but excludes every nonzero homogeneous unitary orbit, so this is not a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the old proof already declares the extension to be L²_loc and uses only compact-time weak identities and mollification. Localizing the standard Duhamel argument is a short, routine function-space repair that preserves the bounded-interval solution class and every substantive conclusion in the affected chain, without a new proof architecture or mathematical loss.

issues.title: Spectral projection is assigned the mollification residual

failure_location.quote: f_n = (i\partial_t - H) u_n = \rho_n \ast (\setindic I f) \xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{} f \quad \text{in $\Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}$},

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then define $u_n(t) = \pi_{(-n, n)}(H) u(t)$ for all $t\in I$.

issues.failure_explanation: For u_n=pi_{(-n,n)}(H)u, commutation with H and the time derivative gives (i∂t-H)u_n=pi_{(-n,n)}(H)f. The old expression rho_n*(1_I f) belongs to the preceding time-mollification sequence and has no asserted equality with the spectral projection residual. Therefore the old proof does not establish convergence in the X_H norm.
dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.overall_effect: The density claim and hence the paper's supplied density-based proof of the integration-by-parts formula are incomplete. The later S-star/PDE connection and L2 variational corollary rely on that formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the spectral-cutoff step, write v_n=π_{(-n,n)}(H)u and replace the residual line by (i∂_t-H)v_n=π_{(-n,n)}(H)f→f in L²(I,H). Invoke commutation of the spectral projector with H and the time derivative, together with strong convergence π_{(-n,n)}(H)→Id, including at t=0, to conclude v_n→u in X_H. This completes the density and integration-by-parts proof and leaves the dependent dual and L² results unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The false copied residual is used to infer convergence in the X_H norm, so correcting it requires an actual spectral-calculus check and is more than a harmless notation change. That check is nevertheless immediate and routine: spectral projectors commute with H and converge strongly, with Bochner-space convergence following by domination. The repair is local, requires no nontrivial new lemma, and preserves all affected statements and guarantees.

issues.title: Corollary-derived ODE minimization has mismatched intervals

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We will compute an approximation of this solution on the time interval $(0,T) = (0, 1)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that Corollary cor: Variational formulation v yields the displayed minimization. That corollary supports a coercive least-squares functional on H1(I) with the residual integrated over the same interval I; in the old context I=(0,1). The display instead takes trials in H1(-1,1) but integrates only over (0,1). Any nonzero h supported in (-1,0) with h(0)=0 leaves the objective unchanged, so the displayed problem lacks the uniqueness and full-space control of the claimed corollary instance.
issues.overall_effect: Only the preliminary claimed derivation is affected: its negative-time component is undetermined. The subsequent weighted full-interval problem is separately stated and supported by its own estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the preliminary corollary-derived minimization, replace the trial space H¹(-1,1) by H¹(0,1), leaving the residual integral over (0,1). Keep the subsequent weighted problem on (-1,1) as the separately introduced full-interval extension.
issues.why_classification: The old source explicitly fixes I=(0,1), and the cited corollary uses the same interval for its trial space and residual. The following prose also says that extension to (-1,1) occurs only in the subsequent weighted problem. Thus H¹(0,1) is uniquely forced, and correcting the trial interval is a transcriptional edit requiring no mathematical repair or change to the later numerical problem.
